title: Python Strings in Practice
description: Work with text using indexing, slicing, methods, and f-strings. The examples use short values so the result is easy to trace.

questions.explanation: String indexes start at zero, so index 1 selects the second character, y.

questions.prompt: Which method removes whitespace from both ends of a string?
questions.explanation: strip removes leading and trailing whitespace. It does not remove spaces between words.

questions.prompt: Strings are immutable, so a string method returns a new string instead of changing the original in place.
questions.explanation: Operations such as upper and replace create a new string value; the original string object is not edited in place.
upper returns a new copy with all alphabetic characters converted to uppercase.

questions.prompt: What does the slice text[1:4] include?
questions.explanation: A slice includes the start index and stops before the end index.
An f-string replaces each expression in braces with its value.
split breaks a string at the separator and returns a list of pieces.

questions.prompt: The in operator can check whether a substring occurs inside a string.
questions.explanation: The in operator checks membership; for example, 'py' in 'python' is True because those characters occur together.
replace returns a new string with the matching text substituted.

questions.prompt: What is the result of len('cat')?
questions.explanation: len counts characters, and cat contains three characters.
